project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 307 (System requires a changelog entry accompanying every book construction change, which returns a validation failure when absent)
project_specification.addition_summary:
Implement app_spec.xml feature 307 in the existing `book` plugin (packages/book, import name book; seat src/app/modules/book): the changelog-entry companion to the authorship guard. The sentence is docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §C8's own closing rule — *"Signal book → IR-weighted combination with shrinkage → volatility targeting → position and concentration limits → orders. Version-controlled, human-authored, explicitly outside the search space. Changing it is a human decision with a changelog entry, not a discovery"* — read on its one clause this package has not yet enforced: a change to the construction is admitted only when it is *accompanied by a changelog entry*, and a change that names no such entry is refused.
Feature 306 built the record this feature builds on: a `BookConstructionChange` already carries the subject, the author, the author kind and the commit. Feature 307 adds the fifth fact §C8 names — the changelog entry — and the refusal that enforces it. Three spellings of one act, all free functions beside the combiner (the shape feature 306's guard and feature 308's cap take — the sentence's whole input is a record the caller already holds, so there is nothing for the factory to compose and nothing for a deployment to configure). `ChangelogEntry` is the entry as its carrier states it: a frozen record of exactly two fields — `subject` (the construction asset the entry documents, a non-empty string) and `body` (the entry's own prose, a non-empty string) — and it is deliberately the entry's own value, not a re-derivation of the change: the entry names its own subject and carries its own body, because the changelog is a document a human writes, not a projection of the change's four fields. `requires_changelog_entry(change, entry)` is the sentence's *requires*: it validates the ask whole first (`ChangelogEntryRequestError`, no code word — a malformed entry names its subject in its first words) and then **raises** `MissingChangelogEntryError` when the change is present and the entry is absent, returning None when both are present. The refusal opens with the greppable code `missing_changelog_entry`, names the change's subject, author, kind and revision, and states the one repair that exists — the human who made the change accompanies it with the changelog entry §C8 requires. `is_missing_changelog_entry(change, entry)` is the read-only spelling — the fact without the refusal — answering True exactly when a change is present and its entry is absent.
The boundary is drawn on presence, not content, and deliberately: this package validates no changelog prose — what the entry *says* is none of this module's business (the authorship guard judges authorship and version control, and the admission gates' business is policy source, not construction records), so the entry is admitted as present when it is a well-stated `ChangelogEntry` and refused as absent when it is not there at all — a `None`, an omission, or a value that could not be stated. The refusal is the sentence's *absent*, and it is the one this module enforces. The ask is total before the judgment: a present entry that is not a well-stated `ChangelogEntry` (a blank subject, a blank body, a non-string field) is refused as `ChangelogEntryRequestError` before any absence is judged, so a caller that handed a broken entry is told *state the entry*, never *the entry is missing*.
No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited; the member joins by workspace-scan convention, adds no `@register`, no table and no endpoint, and imports no other workspace member — the change and the entry arrive as records because a member never re-derives a fact it was handed. The module is stdlib-only at module scope (`dataclasses`, `typing` and the member's own `.errors`), so the factory's scan — which imports this package on every `create_app()` to fire its `@register` — pays nothing for the companion beyond the import it already paid for the guard and the combiner.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (the `book` member already exists: packages/book, import name book; seat src/app/modules/book). The member currently carries features 301, 306 and 308 — `_combine.py` (the IR-weighted `combine` verb, `PromotedSignal`, `CompositeBook`), `_leverage.py` (the quarter-Kelly cap's three verbs and two validators), `_authorship.py` (feature 306's record `BookConstructionChange`, its vocabulary constants, its predicate `is_agent_authored` and its verdict `rejects_agent_authored_modification`) and `errors.py` (the base `BookConstructionError` plus the cap's two siblings and the guard's two siblings), with `__init__.py` holding the one `@register` builder, `build_book_combiner`, under the component name `book`. Feature 307 adds one module and no registration.
existing_context.test_baseline: The book member's own suite under packages/book/tests/ (test_combine, test_leverage, test_authorship, test_component, and this feature's test_changelog). The member is stdlib-only at module scope (the factory's scan imports the package to fire its `@register`, so it must pay nothing), and feature 307's module adds only `dataclasses`, `typing` and the member's own `.errors` to that bill. The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest's testpaths and does NOT collect packages/*/tests (see the acceptance-gate memory), so the member's own suite must be run explicitly as well. Lint only the new files and compare to a sibling — the repo is red on main (mypy absent, ~163 pre-existing ruff errors), so a baseline via `--stdin-filename` misreports.
existing_context.conventions: - One act, one module: `_changelog.py` holds the record, the two validators, the predicate and the verdict; the two refusal classes are added to the existing `errors.py` beside features 301's, 306's and 308's (one place per member, as its docstring already states); `__init__.py` widens its re-export and `__all__` and gains no logic — the shape every member in this workspace takes. - A verdict, not a measurement: the companion judges a change and an entry the caller already holds. It opens no database, reads no environment, consults no clock, touches no filesystem and re-derives neither the change nor the entry — the shape feature 306's `rejects_agent_authored_modification` and feature 308's `rejects_overleveraged_target` take for their own verdicts, and the reason a member never imports another member. - The boundary is presence, not content: the entry is admitted as present when it is a well-stated `ChangelogEntry` and refused as absent when it is not there (`None`, an omission, or a value that could not be stated). This package validates no changelog prose — the entry's subject and body need only be non-empty strings, and what they say is none of this module's business. - Validation is total before any judgment is formed: the entry's two fields are refused in declaration order (subject, body) as `ChangelogEntryRequestError` before any absence is judged, so a present-but-broken entry is told *state the entry* rather than judged missing — the ordering every verdict in this workspace states. - Error vocabulary: two new siblings under `BookConstructionError` (`ChangelogEntryRequestError` for the ask, no code because a malformed ask names its subject in its first words; `MissingChangelogEntryError` for the judgment, opening with `missing_changelog_entry`), so a caller that refuses the whole book surface writes one `except` and a caller that must react differently can still tell the two facts apart — the `BookChangeRequestError` / `AgentAuthoredModificationError` precedent one feature up. - Every refusal message names the facts behind it (the change's subject, author, kind and revision) and cites §C8's rule, so the refusal is actionable without a stack trace; the judgment's message states the one repair that exists (a human accompanies the change with the changelog entry it requires) and does not offer to fabricate one. - Deterministic: pure functions over the two records' fields, so the same change and entry answer identical verdicts and the module holds no state. - Do not edit a central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration (core-task, order-sensitive shared files); no new component is registered, so the composition story is unchanged and `app.order` still carries exactly one `book`.

feature.description: System exposes `ChangelogEntry` — the changelog entry that accompanies a book construction change, as its carrier states it — as a frozen record of exactly two fields: `subject` (the construction asset the entry documents, a non-empty string) and `body` (the entry's own prose, a non-empty string). Construction validates each field in declaration order and refuses with `ChangelogEntryRequestError` what cannot be part of a stated entry: a blank or non-string subject, or a blank or non-string body. The record is the sentence's *changelog entry* made structural — a change that names no entry cannot be accompanied by one — and it carries nothing else: the entry is the human's own document, not a projection of the change's four fields, so its subject is a free name (the asset it documents) and its body is a free string, and neither is re-derived from the change.

System exposes `is_missing_changelog_entry(change, entry)` — the read-only spelling of feature 307's requirement. It validates the ask whole first (the entry's two fields, `ChangelogEntryRequestError`, before any absence is judged — a present-but-broken entry is refused as the ask's own fact, not judged missing), and answers True exactly when a change is present and the entry is absent (`None`, an omitted attribute distinguished from a present-`None` one by sentinel, the combiner's own discipline, so the loader's synthetic-name copies are judged as well as canonical records), and False when a well-stated entry accompanies the change. The shape `book.is_agent_authored` takes for its own fact: validate the ask, answer a fact, and let the caller decide what to do with it.

System exposes `requires_changelog_entry(change, entry)` — the sentence's *requires*. It reads the change's `subject` / `author` / `author_kind` / `revision` surface and the entry's `subject` / `body` surface duck-typed (an absent attribute distinguished from a present-`None` one by sentinel, so the loader's synthetic-name copies are judged as well as canonical records), settles the entry's ask whole in declaration order first (`ChangelogEntryRequestError`, no code word, before any absence is judged), and raises `MissingChangelogEntryError` when a change is present and its entry is absent, returning None when a well-stated entry accompanies the change. The refusal opens with `MISSING_CHANGELOG_ENTRY_CODE` (`missing_changelog_entry`), names the change's subject, author, kind and revision, cites §C8 (*"Changing it is a human decision with a changelog entry, not a discovery"*), and states the one repair that exists: a human makes the change and accompanies it with the changelog entry the sentence requires — the same subject, decided by a person, committed under version control, with the entry that documents it. A refused change forms no value.

System defines the companion's two refusal classes in the member's one error module, as siblings under feature 301's `BookConstructionError` — the one-base-per-member shape the dreaming and regime members state, so a caller that refuses book work wholesale writes one `except` while a caller that must react differently to *the change had no changelog entry* and *your entry could not be stated* catches the specific siblings. `ChangelogEntryRequestError` is the ask's face and carries no code word (a malformed entry names its subject in its first words, the `BookChangeRequestError` / `LeverageRequestError` precedent); it refuses the entry's two fields' own facts before any absence is judged. `MissingChangelogEntryError` is the judgment and opens every message with `missing_changelog_entry`; its repair is its own — a human accompanies the change with the entry — which is why it is its own class and not the base (whose repair is *fix the signals*) or the ask (whose repair is *state the entry*). Both are subclasses of the base and neither of the other; `combine([])` still raises the bare base, so the hierarchy the companion added leaves the old surface reachable.

System keeps the companion a free function beside the combiner rather than a second component: `_changelog.py` is imported by the member's `__init__.py`, which widens its re-export (the record, the one code constant, the predicate, the verdict and the two error classes join features 301's, 306's and 308's names) and gains no `@register`. No new component is composed, `app.order` still carries exactly one `book`, and the seat (src/app/modules/book) is unchanged and still re-exports nothing — a caller that wants the companion reaches the member's own namespace, the discipline every seat in this workspace states. The module is stdlib-only at module scope (`dataclasses`, `typing` and the member's own `.errors`), so the factory's scan — which imports this package on every `create_app()` to fire its `@register` — pays nothing for the companion beyond the import it already paid. No table, endpoint, migration, seat edit, central registry, router, app factory, middleware or settings change. The companion judges a change and an entry the caller hands it; it installs no filesystem hook, writes no changelog file and sweeps no state — the deployment's wiring delivers the change and its entry through the verdict, and this module enforces only that the entry accompanies the change.

System passes the companion over the member's own fixtures: a well-stated `ChangelogEntry` accompanying a change runs (the verdict answers None); a `None` entry, an omitted entry, and a duck-typed stand-in carrying no `body` are each refused with `MissingChangelogEntryError` opening with `missing_changelog_entry` and naming the change's subject, author, kind and revision; a present-but-broken entry (blank subject, blank body, non-string field) is refused at the ask with `ChangelogEntryRequestError` and no code word, and the ask settles before the judgment (a `None` entry paired with a well-stated change meets the judgment; a broken entry meets the ask first); a duck-typed stand-in carrying the entry's two attributes is judged identically to the member's own record (the loader's synthetic-copy trap); an absent change is refused as the ask's own fact, not judged; both error classes are subclasses of `BookConstructionError` and neither of the other; the module is stdlib-only parsed from the AST, imports no other member, opens no store, reads no environment and consults no clock; no verb accepts a content parameter (pinned through `inspect.signature`); and a re-run over the same change and entry answers the identical verdict.

project_specification.integration_points: Feature 307 is the terminal interior node of the Portfolio Book Construction category's authorship chain: `depends_on="306"` is both a code dependency and narrative order — the companion builds on exactly feature 306's `BookConstructionChange` record (it reads the change's four-field surface to name the refusal), and nothing here pre-empts the guard (the companion judges presence of the entry, the guard judges authorship of the change, and the two are independent facts about the same record). The companion imports no other workspace member, and the change's author kinds are read, never borrowed. No `@register` name collides (no new component is registered), no table, endpoint or migration is added, and no central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration is edited.
project_specification.constraints: - No member imports another: the companion takes the change and the entry as records the caller holds; the code and the vocabulary are restated in this member's own terms, never borrowed. - No new component, no `@register`, no seat edit: the companion is a free function beside the combiner, the way feature 306's guard and 308's cap sit. The member's `__init__.py` widens its re-export and carries no logic; the seat still re-exports nothing. - The boundary is presence, not content: the entry is admitted as present when it is a well-stated `ChangelogEntry` and refused as absent when it is not there. This package validates no changelog prose — the entry's subject and body need only be non-empty strings. - Validation is total before any judgment is formed: the entry's two fields (subject, body) are refused as the ask's own class before any absence is judged; only a wholly well-stated entry is judged present or absent. - The verdict reads both records' surfaces duck-typed with an absent-versus-None sentinel, so the loader's synthetic-name copies and any stand-in carrying the surface are judged identically. - Two new error classes, siblings under `BookConstructionError`; the judgment's message opens with the greppable `missing_changelog_entry` and names the change's facts behind it; the ask's carries no code. - Stdlib only (`dataclasses`, `typing`, the member's own `.errors`), no database, no environment, no clock, no filesystem, no state — import-cheap at module scope so the factory's scan pays nothing. - Do not edit a central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings or migration (core-task, order-sensitive shared files).

phase.name: Feature 307 — require a changelog entry accompanying every book construction change
phase.step: 1. `packages/book/src/book/_changelog.py`: the one code constant (`MISSING_CHANGELOG_ENTRY_CODE`), the two validators (`_validated_subject`, `_validated_body`), the record (`ChangelogEntry`, frozen, normalising subject and body), the duck-typed read of both records (`_judged`, sentinels for absence), the refuse-message builder (`_refusal`), and the two public spellings (`is_missing_changelog_entry`, `requires_changelog_entry`). Stdlib only.

2. `packages/book/src/book/errors.py`: add `ChangelogEntryRequestError` and `MissingChangelogEntryError` as siblings under `BookConstructionError`, widen `__all__`, and widen the module docstring with the `missing_changelog_entry` code; update the base class's docstring to name the two new members of the member's refusal surface.

3. `packages/book/src/book/__init__.py`: re-export the record, the one code constant, the predicate, the verdict and the two classes; widen `__all__` (SCREAMING, then Camel, then snake); state in the package docstring that the member now carries features 301, 306, 307 and 308 and that the companion arrives as free functions rather than a second component. Add no `@register`.

4. `packages/book/tests/test_changelog.py`: the admitted path (a well-stated entry accompanying a change runs), the refusal (absent entry refused with the code, naming the change's facts; the message cites §C8 and states the one repair), the ask (present-but-broken entry refused with no code word; the ask settles before the judgment), the duck-typed surface, the error hierarchy, and the layering claims (stdlib-only parsed from the AST, no other member imported, no store or environment or clock, no content parameter in any signature, determinism).

5. `packages/book/tests/test_component.py`: widen the member's `__all__` pin to the four features' names; pin that the companion registers no second component, is reachable without the factory and has no component key, and costs the scan nothing.

6. Validate and run the member's own suite (the repo-level suite under tests/ does not collect packages/*/tests — run the member suite explicitly), confirm the repository-level acceptance suite is unaffected, and lint only the new and changed files against a sibling baseline.

project_specification.success_criteria: - A well-stated `ChangelogEntry` accompanying a book construction change is admitted: `requires_changelog_entry` returns None and `is_missing_changelog_entry` answers False — the path §C8 names, where changing the construction is a human decision *with a changelog entry*. - A change with no accompanying entry is refused with `MissingChangelogEntryError` opening with `missing_changelog_entry` and naming the change's subject, author, kind and revision; the message cites §C8's rule and states the one repair — a human accompanies the change with the entry it requires. - A present-but-broken entry (blank or non-string subject or body) is refused at the ask as `ChangelogEntryRequestError` with no code word, and the ask settles before the judgment even for a change whose entry is absent. - `ChangelogEntryRequestError` and `MissingChangelogEntryError` are both subclasses of `BookConstructionError` and neither of the other; `combine([])` still raises the bare base. - The verdict reads both records' surfaces duck-typed (an absent attribute refused as absent, not read as `None`), so stand-ins and the loader's synthetic copies are judged identically. - No new component is registered (`app.order` carries exactly one `book`), the seat is unchanged, no table, endpoint or migration is added, and no central registry, router, app factory, middleware or settings is edited. - The module is stdlib-only and import-cheap; no verb accepts a content parameter; the member's own suite is green and the repository-level acceptance suite is unaffected.
